export const meta = {
  name: 'review-visibility-implement',
  description: 'Implement PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY slices A/B/C as three parallel workstreams (controller, adapter, UI) in isolated worktrees',
  phases: [{ title: 'Implement', detail: 'controller (Python), server adapter (TS), UI + browser tests, in isolated worktrees' }],
}

const SPEC = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager-ultra/9ef1cac0-1832-43a8-bc1f-712f36914ef4/scratchpad/DESIGN_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md'
const SOURCE = '/home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra'

const REPORT = {
  type: 'object',
  required: ['worktree', 'changed_files', 'tests_run', 'deviations', 'concerns', 'notes_for_integrator'],
  properties: {
    worktree: { type: 'string', description: 'absolute path of the git worktree you worked in (output of `pwd`)' },
    changed_files: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'repo-relative paths you created or modified' },
    tests_run: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', required: ['command', 'result'], properties: { command: { type: 'string' }, result: { type: 'string', description: 'e.g. "59 passed, 0 failed" or the failure summary' } } } },
    deviations: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'places where you departed from the spec and why' },
    concerns: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'bugs, gaps or contract problems you noticed but could not fix within your ownership' },
    notes_for_integrator: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

const common = (stream) => `You are workstream ${stream} of a three-workstream implementation. Work ONLY in your current working directory (it is an isolated git worktree of the md-manager repository; run \`pwd\` first and report it). Do not commit, stash, push or touch any other directory.

STEP 0 (mandatory, before anything else):
1. \`ln -s /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/node_modules node_modules\` (node_modules is gitignored and absent in a fresh worktree).
2. Copy the frozen, already-written contract files from the integrator's checkout into your worktree (they are uncommitted there, so your worktree does not have them yet):
   cp ${SOURCE}/contracts/projects/v1.ts ${SOURCE}/contracts/projects/examples.ts ${SOURCE}/contracts/projects/contract.test.ts ${SOURCE}/contracts/projects/README.md ${SOURCE}/contracts/projects/reviewResult.schema.json ${SOURCE}/contracts/projects/runInputs.schema.json contracts/projects/
   cp ${SOURCE}/contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json contracts/workflow/
   Then run \`npm run test:contracts\` (expect 13 passed) to confirm the copy.
3. Read the design spec at ${SPEC} in full. It is the authoritative description of the shapes shared between workstreams; the PRDs it references are in docs/. Then read the contract files you just copied.

Environment: Python is /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python (never create a venv). Node tooling is in node_modules. Browser tests need no extra setup. Never read or modify ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows (the live run directory), only inspect it read-only if you need a real example of a file shape (its run project-workflows-001 is a real 1.0.0 run with review.json, receipts and packets).

Working discipline: red → green → refactor per increment (write the failing test, observe the behavioural failure, implement, re-run). Keep to your ownership list exactly; if you need a change elsewhere, put it in "concerns" instead of making it. Match the existing code style and the project's fail-closed philosophy. When done, run every test command listed for your workstream and report exact counts. Your final answer must be the structured report (the harness enforces the schema); "changed_files" must be complete.`

phase('Implement')
const results = await parallel([
  () => agent(`${common('P (Python controller, export, CLI, feature directories, docs)')}

YOUR TASK: implement spec section 3 completely (3.1 through 3.8): slice A (native reviewer session with completion-file protocol, third Herdr pane, wait_review, fail-closed acceptance, stop with identity re-check, --reviewer-transport print fallback), the run-state.json 1.2.0 export sections "review" and "inputs" (spec section 2, Python side), the \`workflow export <run>\` CLI action, the review-result and run-inputs feature directories plus launch.py choices, and the docs. Ownership: workflow/** (all .py and .md files), contracts/workflow/README.md, features/project-workflows/README.md, features/review-result/**, features/run-inputs/**. Nothing else.

Order of work: 3.1 settings → 3.2 interactive.py → 3.3 automatic.py → 3.4 pipeline.py → 3.5 export → 3.6 tests (extend as you go, not at the end) → 3.7 features/launch → 3.8 docs. Existing tests must keep passing (59 currently). Run at the end:
  /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python -m unittest workflow.test_automatic workflow.test_interactive workflow.test_feature_launch workflow.test_sessions workflow.test_verification workflow.test_pipeline workflow.test_graph -v
(add your new module, e.g. workflow.test_export, to that list) and report counts. Also sanity-check that \`python -m workflow launch review-result --dry-run\` and \`... run-inputs --dry-run\` print commands. Pay special attention to: no relaunch of a reviewer under any failure; KeyboardInterrupt during wait_review leaves the reviewer running and the receipt at "running"; every rejected completion file is fail-closed; old plans without reviewer_transport still validate; export_state's stability rule; the export CLI must work on a run directory whose worktrees no longer exist (build a lightweight runtime, do not construct InteractiveSessions).`, { label: 'impl:controller', phase: 'Implement', schema: REPORT, isolation: 'worktree' }),

  () => agent(`${common('S (server adapter)')}

YOUR TASK: implement spec section 4 completely: extend the run export schema to versions 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 with the "review" and "inputs" sections (spec section 2), project them onto the frozen contract payloads reviewResult and runInputs (redaction, truncation, requirement_found_in computed only from verbatim substring matches, the review.diff patch artifact served through the artifact route with hash and size checks), the review node's session_id/result_uri in the snapshot, the two new routes with their 404 codes REVIEW_NOT_FOUND / INPUTS_NOT_FOUND and 405 handling, and the tests listed in section 4. Ownership: server/**, config/projects.example.json. Nothing else.

Read server/projects.ts, server/projectRoutes.ts and server/projects.test.ts fully before changing anything; keep the existing 22 tests passing and every existing behaviour (bounded no-follow reads, no paths in messages, contract conformance before sending). Run at the end: \`npx --no-install tsx --test server/projects.test.ts\`, \`npm run test:unit\`, \`npm run test:contracts\`, \`npm run build\`, \`npm run lint\` and report counts. Pay special attention to: the 1.0.0 export (no sections) must still load with the review node's session_id/result_uri null; a malformed section is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID naming only the run; requirement quotes must be matched against the raw task/prompt text before redaction; the diff artifact id is "patch-review-" + the first 12 hex characters of its sha256.`, { label: 'impl:adapter', phase: 'Implement', schema: REPORT, isolation: 'worktree' }),

  () => agent(`${common('U (UI and browser tests)')}

YOUR TASK: implement spec section 5 completely (5.1 through 5.5): the review panel on the review node (slice B), the run inputs (Assignment tab, run header facts, worker node Task / Exact prompt / Launch receipt / Reported-by-the-worker / Handoff / Stop panels), the finding-to-task links with the quote highlight hand-off (slice C), the API client additions, and the mocks, seeds, fixtures and the two new spec files with the nine new scenarios (review-verdict, review-blocked, review-legacy, paths-redacted, run-assignment, worker-inputs, finding-to-task, inputs-legacy, inputs-paths-redacted). Ownership: src/App.tsx, src/App.css, src/graph/**, src/projects/**, src/index.css, tests/project-workflows/**. Nothing else (you may import src/document/Markdown.tsx but not edit it).

Read src/projects/*.tsx, src/projects/api.ts, tests/project-workflows/*.ts and the existing scenarios in projects.spec.ts fully before changing anything; keep the six existing scenarios passing in BOTH phases. IMPORTANT about candidate mode: your worktree's server/ is the OLD adapter (the review and inputs routes are being built in parallel by another workstream), so in candidate mode (WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate) the NINE NEW scenarios are expected to fail against your local backend; write seed.ts exactly per spec section 2 so they pass once the adapter lands, make sure the six existing scenarios still pass in candidate mode, and report the new scenarios' candidate-mode status honestly. Worker mode (mocks) must be fully green: all 15 scenarios. Run at the end: \`npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts\` (worker mode), \`WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts\`, \`npm run build\`, \`npm run lint\`, \`npm run test:unit\` and report counts. Never run two Playwright suites at once. Keep the narrow-layout (420px) assertion in failed-and-paused passing: new panels must not overflow horizontally. Accessibility: headings, labelled tabs (role=tablist/tab/tabpanel with aria-selected/aria-controls), keyboard-operable toggles, and a `<mark>` highlight with visible contrast in both colour schemes (App.css tokens).`, { label: 'impl:ui', phase: 'Implement', schema: REPORT, isolation: 'worktree' }),
])

const [controller, adapter, ui] = results
return { controller, adapter, ui }

tests_run.result: both print the run directory (~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>/<feature>-001) and the preflight/branch/prepare/start(/automatic) command plan; prepare carries --reviewer-transport; nothing executed

tests_run.command: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python -m workflow export <scratchpad copy of ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001 (top-level files + verification/, no worktrees)>
tests_run.result: exit 0: 'Exported run-state.json version 1.2.0 ... No agents launched.' review: transport print, reviewer dd7bdcd1-adec-4efe-bcd4-bbadc3525d95, reviewed_at 2026-09-21T15:42:27.848828Z, diff sha 2bb474561d3e..., 289187 bytes, 6 findings with worker/requirement null; inputs: mode automatic, reviewer_transport native (legacy 4-key plan), launch receipts normalised to Z, completion/handoff/stop for both workers. The live directory was only read; the copy was deleted afterwards

deviations: Print mode now blocks on the contract's rule (P0/P1 not resolved, `blocking_findings`) instead of the previous 'any P0/P1 even if resolved'; both transports share `_decide`, matching `isBlockingFinding` and `check_review`. The existing fake-executable print tests are unaffected (they report no findings).

When a reviewer reports `approved` but carries an unresolved P0/P1, `review.json` is written with `verdict: "blocked"` (the contradictory raw decision is kept in `automatic-review.json.decision`). Writing the reviewer's literal 'approved' would make review.json fail both `check_review(require_approved=False)` and the TS `validateReviewResult` cross-field rule, so the export would refuse the run.

The shared review prompt's 'Requirements:' sentence is generalised to point at the worker tasks pinned in plan.json (nodes.<worker>.task) plus the feature/contract READMEs they cite, because the reviewer now has to quote task text verbatim and the prompt is no longer specific to features/project-workflows.

A failed `run_reviewer` launch records `automatic-review.json` status `needs_reconciliation` (with the error) rather than `blocked`, and no stop is attempted, because the session identity is unknown at that point; the next `drive` raises the reconciliation error and never relaunches (spec only covered wait-phase failures).
`InteractiveSessions.status()` also reports the reviewer when `review.interactive.json` exists (small addition for operator inspection).

`FakeSessions.run` now writes a fuller worker receipt (launch_requested_at, launcher_invocations, background_id, ...) so the pipeline test's export carries `inputs.workers.*.launch`; the automatic graph tests count reviewer launches via `fake-launches.log` so the cross-process tests can assert exactly one launch.
`wait_review` resolves `clock`/`sleep` at call time (None defaults) instead of binding `time.time` at definition, so the deadline test can patch `workflow.automatic.time`.

`export_run` uses the prepare-shaped state (`next: [launch_ui, launch_adapter]`) when `pipeline.sqlite` does not exist, i.e. for a prepared-but-never-started run, instead of creating an empty database in the run directory.
concerns: Stop failure after acceptance: per the spec order the receipt is marked `succeeded` before `stop_reviewer()`; if that stop then fails, the review node records a task error while the receipt stays `succeeded`, so a later `retry` returns the review without re-attempting the stop and the operator must stop the reviewer by its exact ID (documented in the RUNBOOK). Reordering (stop before succeeded) or re-checking `review.stop.json` on resume would close this; I kept the spec order.

For workstream S: the exported `inputs` section carries fields the TS `runInputs` payload does not (`launch.launch_token`, `launch.background_id`, `setup[].argv`, `checks[].argv`, `failure_drill`, `policy_version`, and `workers` as a dict keyed by lane), exactly as spec section 2 shows; the adapter must project/drop them rather than validate the export section with the payload schema.

A worker `completion.json`/`handoff.json` whose `open_assumptions` contains an empty string exports as `null` (treated as malformed, since the contract requires non-empty strings); the alternative was failing the whole run in the adapter. Documented in the feature README as 'malformed optional receipt → null'.

The live smoke test from PRD slice A section 5 (real `claude --bg` reviewer in a scratch run with a copy of project-workflows-001's bundle, pane appearing, completion file written, `claude stop`) was not performed here; offline tests cover the protocol with FakeSessions only. Real flags to watch: `--allowedTools Write(//<abs path>)` semantics under `--permission-mode dontAsk` and whether `--add-dir` grants Read of plan.json/review-bundle.json in the run directory.
`Pipeline.report()` (every CLI boundary) now hashes `review.diff` on each export; acceptable per spec but visible on very large diffs.

The step-0 contract copies (contracts/projects/{v1.ts,examples.ts,contract.test.ts,README.md,reviewResult.schema.json,runInputs.schema.json}, contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json) exist uncommitted in this worktree as byte-identical copies of the integrator's files; they are not listed in changed_files because this workstream did not author or modify them. The `node_modules` symlink is gitignored.
controller.notes_for_integrator: Ownership respected: only workflow/**, contracts/workflow/README.md, features/project-workflows/README.md and the two new feature directories were edited. Key shapes: `review.interactive.json` (node_id review, launch_token, plan_digest, worktree, base_commit, candidate_commit, status, attempt, launcher_invocations, launch_requested_at, then background_id/session_id/observed_state/native_started_at); `automatic-review.json` native = {transport, launch_token, bundle_sha256, candidate_commit, patch_sha256, status launching→running→succeeded|blocked|needs_reconciliation, session_id, background_id, decision, review, accepted_at, error}; print receipts gain `transport: print`, `decision`, `accepted_at`. Events: review/running 'Launching the native reviewer session', review/interactive 'Reviewer session <uuid> launched; awaiting review.completion.json', review/running 'Reviewer pane attached|not attached: ...' (only when terminals.json exists and HERDR_ENV=1), review/interrupted (resume note), review/stopped, review/approved. `check_review(review, bundle, digest, require_approved=...)` and `blocking_findings` are module functions in pipeline.py; `Pipeline.validate_review(review, require_approved=True)` wraps them; `ExportRuntime` + `export_run` back the `export` CLI. `export_state` derives `review`/`inputs` exactly per spec section 2 (see the runtime storage seam in features/project-workflows/README.md for the written-out shape); `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"`. After merge run `.venv/bin/python -m workflow export ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001` (verified on a copy; it will bump updated_at once, then stay stable). `launch.py` features: project-workflows, review-result, run-inputs; `--run-id` defaults to <feature>-001 and the run root to ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/<feature>. Verbose logs of the counted runs are in the scratchpad as wsP-final-tests.log.

tests_run.result: 28 passed, 0 failed (22 existing + 6 new; red run before implementation: 8 failed for the expected reasons - 1.2.0 export rejected as RUN_STORAGE_INVALID, new routes NOT_FOUND)
tsc -b (covers server/** and tests/**) + vite build succeeded, exit 0

deviations: Sections are honoured whenever present regardless of `version`: the export schema accepts versions 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 and `review`/`inputs` as nullable-optional keys, but does not reject e.g. a 1.0.0 export that carries a `review` key (the section is still validated strictly). Spec section 2 describes the producer's version/key pairing; I chose not to make the adapter fail a run over it.

Timestamps in the sections (`reviewed_at`, `launch.launch_requested_at`, `stop.confirmed_at`) accept any ISO offset and are normalised to a trailing Z (`+00:00` is rewritten preserving microseconds; other offsets go through Date and keep millisecond precision). Spec said `reviewed_at` is passed through; it is unchanged for Z input.

Redaction runs before truncation for task/prompt texts (so a cut can never expose a partial path); the marker's `N more characters` therefore counts characters of the redacted text. A cut that would split a surrogate pair moves one code unit back.

`reviewer.session_id` (and the snapshot review node's `session_id`) and `inputs.feature` also pass through `redactPaths` (identity for UUIDs, e-mail style identities and ordinary names) to honour the no-paths rule; spec said pass-through.
Blank `open_assumptions` entries in `completion`/`handoff` are dropped, mirroring the existing worker-result projection, instead of failing the run against the contract's min(1) rule.
The review node's `attempt` is set from the review section's `attempt` alongside `session_id`/`result_uri` (spec listed only the latter two; status logic is unchanged).
Diff artifact: a registered `bytes` that differs from the file length is refused as ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH (message says 'hash or size'); the bounded read still maps to ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE.

Sections are projected eagerly in projectRun, so a cross-field contradiction (approved review with an unresolved P0/P1, automatic mode with null settings, duplicate check IDs, etc.) is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID for detail, list and the new routes alike; the routes additionally re-run validateReviewResult/validateRunInputs before conform (a failure there would be RESPONSE_INVALID, never expected).

`inputs.workers` keys are restricted to the contract's WORKER_LANES (`ui`, `adapter`) via z.partialRecord and must be non-empty; a foreign lane makes the run RUN_STORAGE_INVALID. `diff.path` must be exactly `review.diff`.
concerns: For workstream P (export_state.py): the adapter's strict section schemas require `review.diff.path == "review.diff"`, timezone-aware ISO timestamps (naive strings are rejected), `launch.native_started_at` as an integer epoch-ms or null, `completion.summary`/`handoff.summary` non-empty (spec says a malformed completion file becomes null; an empty summary should be treated as malformed), `checks[].kind` within build/typecheck/unit/integration/contract/browser, browser checks with scenarios and non-browser checks without, `owned_paths` relative, and worker lanes limited to `ui`/`adapter`. Any extra key in a section fails the run (strictObject).

For workstream U (seed.ts/mock.ts): the diff artifact id is `patch-review-` + first 12 hex chars of the sha256 of review.diff's bytes, served text/plain inline with nosniff/CSP; `requirement_found_in` is empty for every finding when the export has no `inputs` section (1.1.0), and a quote is matched against the raw task text (falling back to the prompt only when the task is an empty string).

The live run's plan.json has `mode: "interactive"` while the spec derives `inputs.mode` from the presence of `plan.automatic`; the adapter only accepts `automatic`/`manual` in the section, so P must map it as the spec says.

Error text from zod issues is forwarded through invalidRun (redacted); it never includes input values in the cases tested, but a future contract regex whose message embeds the value would rely on redactPaths alone.
adapter.notes_for_integrator: Nothing outside server/** was changed; config/projects.example.json is untouched. The contracts/* entries in `git status` are the frozen files copied in step 0 and verified byte-identical to /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra (diff -q reported same for all seven). Implementation summary: server/projects.ts extends exportSchema (versions 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0; strict `review`/`inputs` sub-schemas per spec section 2), projects them eagerly in projectRun onto ReviewResult/RunInputs (LoadedRun gains `review`, `inputs`, `reviewDiff`), computes requirement_found_in from verbatim raw-text substring matches only, registers the review diff as `patch-review-<sha12>` served through RunStore.artifact beside packet artifacts with hash+size checks, and gives the review node session_id/result_uri (+attempt) from the section only (never from `values`). server/projectRoutes.ts adds GET .../runs/:run_id/reviews/:attempt (404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND, 400 INVALID_ATTEMPT) and GET .../runs/:run_id/inputs (404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND); both are in the `paths` map so the existing loop gives them 405+Allow and Fastify's automatic HEAD. server/projects.test.ts: writeRun accepts `version`, `review`, `inputs`, `diffFile`; fixtures reviewSection/inputsSection/workerInput; six new tests (review projection+links, diff artifact, blocked review, 1.0.0/1.1.0/null sections, inputs projection incl. 65536-char truncation marker and Z normalisation, 28 malformed-section cases) plus the 405/HEAD/no-write test and the contract-conformance test extended to the new routes. No app.ts change was needed.
